items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So when my first contact with the orchestra was made... Monsieur Pango had his office... Monsieur Pango plays alto, accordion and organ, but he didn't take any part in the numbers I rehearsed for the concerts.

ctx.x: So when my first contact with the orchestra was made, it happened in Treichville, a suburb of Abidjan, the second day after my arrival. There was a reception for Lily and I in the building where Monsieur Pango had his office and then we went to a one room place near-by for the rehearsal. The line up of the orchestra was three trumpets, one alto, one tenor, two clarinets, two electric accompaniment guitars, one electric bass guitar, a drummer, a tom-tom player, a male singing quartet, and a female choir of eight.…

The musicians were mostly young students from different parts of the country and were not very much in the know about jazz, but they loved it & were very cooperative. They had rehearsed in advance standards such as 'Perdido', 'Basin Street Blues', 'St. Louis Blues'. We rehearsed also a couple of Negro Spirituals with the male singing quartet and this was going to be a big success. A couple of the musicians could speak a little English, but I speak French not too badly and as French is the national language spoken…
